title: Senator Rosilicie Ochoa Bogh highlights community engagement in San Bernardino County - East SBV Times
text:
Senator Rosilicie Ochoa Bogh, who represents California’s 23rd Senate District, recently shared updates on her official X account regarding meetings and community events in San Bernardino County.
On September 29, 2025, Senator Ochoa Bogh posted about a meeting with the wife of a prominent local law enforcement figure. She wrote, “It was an honor to meet with Kelli Boatwright, the wife of Undersheriff Boatwright, a true pillar of public service in San Bernardino County. Undersheriff Boatwright dedicated his life to public safety, mentorship, and uplifting his community — both in uniform and beyond.”
Later that day, she expressed gratitude for an update on a major regional infrastructure project. In her post from September 29, 2025, Senator Ochoa Bogh stated, “Thank you for taking the time to update me and my team on the Gold Line Project and the board’s recent decision. Your insight into the history, funding challenges, and governance issues was invaluable, and I greatly appreciate the clarity you provided. @goSBCTA” The Gold Line Project is a significant transportation initiative in Southern California aimed at expanding light rail service into San Bernardino County. The project has faced various funding obstacles and governance complexities over several years as it seeks to improve regional transit options.
In another post from September 29, 2025, Senator Ochoa Bogh congratulated Crafton Hills College on a new campus facility: “Congrats to Crafton Hills College on the opening of the Finkelstein Performing Arts Center! This new building is more than a beautiful addition to the campus. It is a cultural home where creativity is nurtured, diverse voices are uplifted, and our shared humanity is celebrated.” Crafton Hills College serves students throughout San Bernardino County by providing academic programs and community resources.
Senator Ochoa Bogh has been active in highlighting local achievements and ongoing projects within her district through social media communications.
